item.title: Shadow Creek and quarterback Tavis Coleman end Pearland's 19-game winning streak in regular season
item.description: Shadow Creek quarterback Tavis Coleman throws under pressure by Pearland linebacker Terrence Spriggs during a high school football game at Freedom Field in Rosharon, Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) IOWA COLONY - Shadow Creek quarterback Tavis Coleman hasn't made many mistakes this season. But when his first pass of the game on Friday night was intercepted, he understood exactly how he needed to respond. He wasn't going to hang his head or get frustrated. He was going to use it as fuel. On the Sharks' very next offensive snap, the senior signal-caller delivered. He threw a 60-yard touchdown pass to sophomore sensation B.J. LaFell, shrugging off the early miscue and igniting a Shadow Creek fireworks show. "You have to have a dog mentality," Coleman said. "I told myself that was personal, so I went back out there, executed and threw a touchdown to my teammate, so that's all that matters. It was good." SCOREBOARD: Friday's area and state scores Coleman was lights-out the rest of the night, completing 19-of-23 passes for a season-high 361 yards and four touchdowns. He also rushed for a score during the Sharks' 55-35 victory over Pearland at Freedom Field, a triumph that clinched at least a share of the District 19-6A championship with one game remaining before the playoffs. Shadow Creek (8-1, 7-0), which entered the night No. 9 in the Class 6A state rankings, has won seven consecutive games since dropping a non-district contest against No. 4 Ridge Point early in the season. The Sharks also avenged a 21-14 loss to Pearland (8-1, 6-1) from last year and ended the Oilers' 19-game regular-season winning streak. Shadow Creek has now won seven district championships since its inaugural season in 2018. But while that's certainly a goal every year, making a deep push in the playoffs means even more. In a game that had its share of ups and downs, Sharks coach Tyrone Green was pleased with how his team responded to some of the adversity and believes his group has what it takes to make some noise once the calendar flips to November. "I took away that they pull for each other," said Green, now in his third season at the helm. "We had some things that happened early on with Pearland scoring. But we were able to come back offensively and get scores, get scores. So they pulled for each other, they're together, and that's the biggest thing that I saw from this game." item.title: Jonathan Law football holds off Shelton comeback as Matthew Witteman accounts for six TDs
item.description: Jonathan Law quarterback Mathew Witteman runs through the Shelton defense in the second half on October 30, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) SHELTON - The Jonathan Law football team built a 27-point lead in the third quarter before holding off Shelton 41-35 in a thriller Friday night at Finn Stadium. Matthew Witteman led the way by accounting for six scores, including five touchdown passes to five different receivers. He added an 8-yard TD run. "In the [passing game], wide receivers were just winning their ones and making my job really easy," Witteman said. In the first quarter, after Shelton scored first on a 1-yard touchdown run by Cole St. Pierre, Witteman and the Lawmen offense marched down the field and capped off the drive with a 7-yard touchdown catch from Hunter Kendzierski on a slant. Witteman added touchdown passes of 30 and 5 yards to give the Lawmen a 21-7 lead at halftime. "He's awesome," Law head coach Ryan Pearson said. "He's a hard worker. He's earned all of this stuff, all of the credit he's gotten." Witteman continued his production in the second half with touchdown passes of 46 and 70 yards and his touchdown run. Then, Shelton made a comeback. The Gaels were without starting quarterback Jackson Hyner in the first half due to a team-related issue, and the Gaels' offense struggled without him. When Hyner returned in the second half, Shelton stormed back by scoring 21 unanswered points after being down 41-14 midway through the third quarter. "Third quarter, we started out hot, but got brought back to life a little bit," Pearson said. "It's good to see our kids fight to the very end, but I'd like to see it get a little cleaner." Hyner scored on a 26-yard touchdown run to make the score 41-21. Then, Shelton's defense made a crucial stop after struggling against Law's offense for much of the game. After a bad snap on a Law punt gave Shelton the ball inside Law's 30-yard line, the Gaels put together a short drive capped by a 1-yard touchdown run by St. Pierre. Shelton came up big defensively again by getting an interception and forcing a fumble on back-to-back drives. After the fumble, Hyner connected with Evan Boutellier for a 23-yard TD pass, making it 41-35. "We started falling apart a little bit, but I brought all the guys together and made sure we were on the same page," Witteman said. Shelton had a chance to take the lead with less than two minutes left in the fourth quarter, but the Lawmen's defense was able to make the fourth-down stop. Law was able to run the clock out after a Shelton penalty gave it a first down. Law, which improved to 5-2, hosts North Haven next Friday at 7 p.m., while Shelton (4-3) plays at Notre Dame-West Haven at 6:30 p.m. Player of the Game Matthew Witteman, Jonathan Law: Witteman accounted for six touchdowns, including five in the air to five different receivers. item.title: Mike Tomlin reportedly has one major reason to stay away from NFL return
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Mike Tomlin is reportedly not guaranteed to return to NFL coaching in 2027 despite being expected to attract significant interest from teams looking for a new head coach. The former Pittsburgh Steelers coach has made a strong start to his broadcasting career with NBC after stepping away from the sidelines following 19 seasons in charge of the franchise. However, a return to coaching would mean giving up a role that offers him a more relaxed schedule and considerably less pressure than the demands of leading an NFL team. Mike Tomlin’s new NBC role could keep him away from NFL coaching According to Front Office Sports , Tomlin is enjoying his work as a studio analyst and is not necessarily prepared to leave it behind for another coaching opportunity. One source told the publication: “Money has nothing to do with this. … Of course [NFL teams] are going to offer him stuff. The question is: Is he having a good time doing what he’s doing and is he good at it?” Tomlin has quickly established himself as a popular voice on NBC’s Sunday Night Football coverage, with his direct opinions and trademark expressions attracting attention. He has also started a YouTube channel to share his interest in Minecraft, giving him more time to pursue interests outside football. That is a significant change from his previous role with the Steelers, where he never recorded a losing season across 19 years as head coach. Tomlin led Pittsburgh to the playoffs 13 times and reached the Super Bowl twice, winning the championship once. His experience and record mean he is expected to rank among the leading candidates if teams make coaching changes. The New York Jets and Washington Commanders have emerged as potential destinations in the speculation surrounding his future. However, both situations could require him to take charge of teams facing significant challenges. There is also a potential contractual complication. Tomlin signed an extension with Pittsburgh through the 2027 season, although it is unclear whether the team has exercised its option for that year. The Steelers could therefore retain contractual rights that might require another franchise to compensate them if it wanted to hire him. For now, Tomlin has given no public indication that he intends to return to coaching. With his broadcasting career already gathering momentum, NFL teams may need to offer more than an attractive salary to convince him to leave the studio. item.title: ‘Vintage LeBron (James),’ ‘Obvious Goaltend’ — NBA World Reacts as 41-Year-Old 76ers Star’s Chase-Down Block Shows He’s Still Got It
item.description: LeBron James chases down OG Anunoby for a block, but the play quickly divides fans over a possible goaltending call. LeBron James gave the world another reminder of what he can still do at 41 during Friday night’s 98-93 win over the New York Knicks. A defensive play in the third quarter brought the crowd to its feet and drew plenty of attention online, although not everyone agreed with the officials’ decision. LeBron James’ Block on OG Anunoby Draws Mixed Reactions The four-time MVP chased down Knicks forward OG Anunoby and blocked his shot off the backboard during the Philadelphia Sixers’ NBA Cup opener at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Hoop Central shared a clip with the caption “LeBron James chase down block,” adding, “Vintage LeBron.” The Athletic’s Fred Katz also praised the play : “LeBron James, at age 41, is still smashing chase-down blocks against backboards.” One fan disagreed , replying to Katz: “Obvious goaltend.” Sports and political analyst Andy Froemel was also among those impressed : “LeBron James with the chase-down block at 41 years old, no problem.” Basketball account Hoop Muse acknowledged the defensive effort but questioned the call: “Great block but goaltend (hard to see in real time though).” Not everyone thought the play was particularly eye-catching. Another fan wrote that “Anunoby has one of the lowest vert in the league” and added, “This is NOT impressive.” One viewer brought up James’ approaching birthday: “Turns 42 next month.” The viewer was a month early. James was born Dec. 30, 1984, and will turn 42 in December. His ability to make a play like that at his age was part of what drew so much attention. The officials allowed the block, which was James’ only one of the game. Philadelphia finished with 4 blocks, compared with 2 for New York. The disagreement centered on whether the play met the NBA’s definition of goaltending. Under NBA rules, goaltending includes touching a shot on its downward flight when it has a chance to score. It also applies when a defender touches a shot that still has a chance to go in after it strikes the backboard above the rim. The play was officially ruled a block, though some viewers argued it met the criteria for goaltending. The play came just two nights after James was on the receiving end of a similar block. Indiana Pacers two-way forward Jalen Slawson caught him from behind on a transition layup during Philadelphia’s 114-109 win Wednesday. The Pacers successfully challenged the original foul call. item.title: Senators’ Hayden Hodgson gets 2-game suspension for charging Kings’ Brandt Clarke
item.description: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Senators’ Hayden Hodgson gets 2-game suspension for charging Kings’ Brandt Clarke appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ottawa Senators forward Hayden Hodgson has been suspended for two games , without pay, for boarding Los Angeles Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke during Thursday’s matchup. After conducting a disciplinary hearing with Hodgson, the NHL’s Department of Player Safety announced its ruling on Friday. The incident occurred during the second period of Ottawa’s game against Los Angeles at Crypto.com Arena. Hodgson approached Clarke at approximately 21 miles per hour, according to the game broadcast. The Kings defenseman was retrieving the puck near his own net when Hodgson crashed into him, sending Clarke headfirst into the boards. The 30-year-old received a five-minute major penalty and a game misconduct, ending his involvement in the contest. Clarke subsequently left the game with an upper-body injury and did not return. However, he participated in the team’s practice session Friday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The suspension comes with a financial penalty for Hodgson. Under the NHL’s collective bargaining agreement, he will surrender $8,762.88 in salary, with the money directed toward the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. This is not the first time Hodgson has faced disciplinary action for boarding. In October 2025, the league fined him $2,018.23, the maximum permitted under the collective bargaining agreement, after checking Montreal Canadiens forward Alex Newhook during a preseason game. He also received a game misconduct for that incident. Hodgson has appeared in just 24 NHL games across five seasons with the Philadelphia Flyers and the Senators, recording one goal and three points. He has accumulated 51 penalty minutes at the NHL level, while his disciplinary record also includes 20 games worth of suspensions in the American Hockey League over the past five seasons for elbowing and other offenses . As a result of his latest suspension, Hodgson will miss Ottawa’s road games against the San Jose Sharks on Saturday and the Anaheim Ducks on Sunday. He is eligible to return Wednesday versus the Buffalo Sabres. Meanwhile, the Senators have recalled forwards Xavier Bourgault and Philip Tomasino from their AHL affiliate, Belleville.

item.title: High school football: Pleasant Grove unfazed by bad weather in convincing 5A first round win at Spanish Fork
item.description: Cold and rainy conditions like what Spanish Fork and Pleasant Grove had to play through on Friday night usually favor the defenses. Surprisingly though, Pleasant Grove’s offense was unfazed by the wet weather, which ultimately paved the way for some sweet redemption for the Vikings. After narrowly losing to Spanish Fork back in Week 6, No. 10 seed Pleasant Grove used a strong second quarter in the 5A first round rematch to pull away from the seventh-seeded Dons for the impressive 34-10 victory. “I think the guys battled hard tonight. I think they were hungry. I think they were ready to go, but it always comes down to execution,” said Pleasant Grove coach Jeremy Lapan. “I thought our guys executed at a high level, made the catches. Offensive line blocked phenomenally. The O-line doesn’t get enough credit. They’ve developed so much.” That strong offensive line play allowed quarterback Cannon Jacobson to pass for two touchdowns, while Corbin Robbins tallied a rushing and a receiving TD in the victory. With the victory, Pleasant Grove advances to next week’s 5A quarterfinals against No. 2 seed and defending state champ Orem. It’s a rematch of Orem’s 35-10 win over Pleasant Grove back in Week 8. “Hopefully we can come ready to play. That’s a really good football team,” said Lapan. “Hopefully we can show that we’ve developed a little bit and got better.” While Spanish Fork’s offense clearly struggled with consistency in the difficult conditions Friday, Lapan said he didn’t make any adjustments to his play calling, believing his team prepared for the conditions as best it could with hand warmers, towels and ponchos. Lapan said he called five trick plays during the game, but was immediately prepared to audible out of those calls if he could sense the players were nervous about ball security. He could see in their eyes they never were. “We probably spent $1,000 on hand warmers and ponchos and towels to keep those balls dry. In these conditions, it is a huge deal to keep your hands warm and to keep the ball dry,” said Lapan. With Pleasant Grove leading 6-3 midway through the second quarter after both offenses settled for early field goals, the Vikings found their rhythm offensively late in the frame. Robbins scored on a 5-yard run with 4:50 left in the first half, pushing the lead to 13-3, and then with 10 seconds left in the half he scored again on a 8-yard TD pass from Jacobson for the 20-3 halftime lead. After both offenses stalled on their opening drives of the third quarter, Spanish Fork put together its best drive of the game as quarterback Nixon Warren capped an 80-yard scoring drive with a 4-yard sweep just inside the pylon, cutting the deficit to 20-10 with 1:27 left in the third. item.title: Serie A Preview: Milan vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Milan vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction One of the most interesting fixtures in the Serie A calendar takes place at San Siro this weekend as Milan take on their fiercest rivals, Inter. The latest edition of the famous Derby della Madonnina could already determine the fate of Milan’s faint title hopes. Despite going unbeaten in his first eight league games in charge of Milan (W5, D3), Ruben Amorim is responsible for the club’s second-weakest start to the season since 2019/20. Only 18 points from the opening nine rounds left the Rossoneri seven points adrift of joint leaders Inter and Lazio ahead of the weekend. With that in mind, anything other than a win in this mouth-watering showdown would likely spell the end of Milan’s pursuit of their landmark 20th Scudetto. However, it’s easier said than done, especially given Inter’s form heading into this meeting. Cristian Chivu’s men have enjoyed a near-flawless start to their title defense. Inter left it late to beat out-of-sorts Venezia in midweek Serie A action, as two own goals from the Winged Lions beyond the 75th minute propelled them to a 2-0 victory. The Nerazzurri have dropped points once so far this season (W8, D1) and are currently level on points with Lazio and four clear of third-placed Roma. Match Preview Milan Amorim’s unbeaten Serie A record ended abruptly on Wednesday as Bologna thrashed Milan 4-2 at San Siro despite trailing by a goal at halftime. Raffaele Palladino’s side brutally exposed Milan’s defensive frailties, which have seen the Rossoneri concede at least two goals in three of their last four games across all competitions. San Siro has been anything but a fortress this term, with two of Amorim’s three defeats at the helm coming at this stadium (W3). If it’s any consolation, Milan have scored two or more goals in four of their five competitive home outings in 2026/27, except for a dismal 2-0 loss to Benfica in the Europa League. item.description: Philadelphia's LeBron James drives against Karl-Anthony Towns in the 76ers' NBA Cup group stage victory over the New York Knicks (Emilee Chinn) LeBron James scored 20 points including a late tip-in to help seal the Philadelphia 76ers' 98-93 victory over the NBA champion New York Knicks on Friday. The 76ers notched their second win of the young season over the Knicks after spoiling their championship banner-raising with a victory at Madison Square Garden on opening night. The win had a double edge as Friday's games marked the start of the fourth edition of the NBA Cup, the NBA in-season tournament won by the Knicks before they went on to beat the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals for their first championship since 1973. Group-stage Cup games will be played throughout November, all counting in the regular-season standings. Quarter-finals will be played December 4-5 and semi-finals December 8-9 before the final on December 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana. Tyrese Maxey scored 27 points to lead the Sixers, who took control early against the sloppy Knicks. They led by 14 in the third quarter and weathered a late Knicks surge. Jalen Brunson's step-back three-pointer put New York up 90-89 with 1:32 remaining. James, the NBA's all-time leading scorer, answered with a basket that put Philadelphia back in front and pushed the lead to 96-91 with a tip-in off a Maxey miss with 11.9 seconds left. James, 41, added nine rebounds, eight assists, one steal and a vintage chase-down block in what 76ers coach Nick Nurse called his best game since joining as a free agent in June. "I thought he was really good all the way through," Nurse said. "When we got some downhill stuff he used his size and knocked them around a little bit for some layups... kind of pushed and organized it. "He's been good, but that was his best game, for sure." Brunson led New York with 24 points and Karl-Anthony Towns added 22 points and 12 rebounds for the Knicks, who fell to 2-4. The Rockets had emerged from a back-and-forth first half with a 51-44 lead, pushing the advantage to as many as 11 before taking an eight-point lead into the final frame. item.title: Ducati copies swingarm fins and Aprilia responds with upgraded version
item.description: Motorsport photo MotoGP is moving towards a new set of technical regulations that will reduce the influence of aerodynamics, but that does not mean manufacturers have stopped experimenting with new solutions in this area. Until a few years ago, motorcycles featured little more than simple wings, but aerodynamic development has been relentless since then. First came the stepped fairings, followed by tail fins, which became the next frontier as they are not subject to homologation under the current regulations, allowing manufacturers to develop them without restrictions. The same applies to fork wings and seat wings, which have gradually appeared on the bikes of every manufacturer. Now, attention appears to have shifted towards the swingarms, which have increasingly been covered by aerodynamic fairings. Aprilia, however, has opened up another avenue of development. At Silverstone, when MotoGP returned from its summer break, two new vertical fins appeared on the RS-GP, extending upwards from the rear section of the swingarm (pictured above). The likely purpose is to help manage the turbulence generated by the rear wheel, which has long been one of the biggest challenges for aerodynamicists. Aprilia has continued to use the solution regularly since its introduction, and it has now seemingly inspired a rival manufacturer. At Phillip Island last weekend, a similar design appeared on Marc Marquez's Ducati. Evidently, Ducati engineers have studied their rival's solution closely and concluded that it could also work well on the Desmosedici GP. The results must have been encouraging, as Marquez continued to use it during the opening day of practice at Sepang (pictured below), where he topped both sessions. Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Marc Marquez, Ducati Team Aprilia, however, has no intention of standing still. A further evolution of the concept arrived in Malaysia, with a new version fitted to Marco Bezzecchi's RS-GP. The updated design could be described as an angled L-shape, extending not only upwards but also towards the rear of the motorcycle (pictured in the main image). The fact that manufacturers are continuing to develop these solutions with just four rounds remaining in the current regulatory era suggests they could also prove useful in 2027. After all, the aerodynamic restrictions for next year primarily concern lateral dimensions, whereas this particular component protrudes considerably less than the widest sections of the fairing. Furthermore, the 850cc regulations will also require homologation for tail units, but make no mention of swingarms. Could this therefore become an important area of aerodynamic development – and a new battleground – next season? item.title: Raptors Scottie Barnes Sets Career High in Points Against Magic
item.description: Scottie Barnes Raptors Magic Getty Toronto Raptors superstar Scottie Barnes set a career-high in points against the Orlando Magic in Friday night’s NBA Cup group play game. Barnes and the Raptors lost the game 121-114, but Barnes had a terrific individual game to remember in defeat. Scottie Barnes Scores 41 Points for Raptors Against the Magic, Barnes had 41 points for the Raptors, which is a career-high for him. Barnes was 19-of-34 from the field and 2-of-3 from the free-throw line for the Raptors, while also adding 5 rebounds and 5 assists. Scottie Barnes despite losing to the Magic: 41 PTS19-34 FG5 REB2 STL pic.twitter.com/0eFo3su0rT — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 31, 2026 Unfortunately for Barnes and the Raptors, the points did not help the team win, as they lost to the Magic on their home court, just two nights after blowing Orlando out at home on the first night of a home-and-home set against the Magic. But on Friday, the tables were turned as the Magic were far superior to the Raptors in almost every facet of the game. Though the Raptors made a late comeback and nearly came back to win, they climbed into too big a hole early, which made it difficult to successfully come back and win late. Raptors Have Been Average This Year It’s only five games into the season, but the Raptors have been just average this year, as the team has a 3-2 record so far. While they have looked like an elite team at times, they have not looked great at other times, and until this team can play with more consistency, it’s hard to think that they are true contenders in the Eastern Conference. To be fair to Toronto, they are missing superstar Kawhi Leonard , who is out for a few weeks with a knee injury, and anytime you are missing your best player in the NBA, it’s difficult to win. But still, Raptors head coach Darko Rajakovic would surely love his team to play with a little more consistency and show that they can win games on a consistent basis without Leonard in the team’s lineup. For now, they will look to flush this disappointing loss to Orlando and gear up for their next game against the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday.
